title: Tennis: serve
rulebook: ITF Rules of Tennis 2024: Rule 1 (the court), Rule 3 and Appendix I (the ball), Rule 4 and Appendix II (the racket), Rule 12 (a ball on a line), Rules 16-19 (the service, its order, the foot fault, the service fault), Rule 22 (the let)
deviations: Rules 5-11, 20, 23-26 (the point): one first serve only, with no receiver; a fault ends the attempt as a failure (there is no second serve after a fault), a good serve ends it as the success
Rule 22 (the let is replayed, as often as it happens): a let is replayed 1 time(s), with the spare ball that waits in a cup on a stand 0.6 m to your left; a further let ends the attempt as a failure

Rule 16 ('stand at rest ... immediately before starting the service motion'): made measurable: both feet on the ground and neither moved more than 0.02 m during the 0.5 s before the ball leaves the hand; the service motion is the time from that release to the racket's strike

Rule 18 a ('slight movements of the feet are permitted', no walking or running): made measurable: during the service motion no foot may touch the ground more than 0.3 m from where it stood at the release

Rule 19 Case 1 (a toss that the server does not try to hit may be caught or let drop and tossed again): the intention cannot be judged and the hand takes the ball only once: one toss per serve; a tossed ball that reaches the ground unstruck is a fault

Rule 16 (release 'by hand'): the hand's grip is a weld that is switched off; so that a ball struck out of the hand is not a serve, the ball must have been touching nothing of you for 0.1 s when the racket strikes it

Rule 16 ('hit the ball with the racket'): so that a ball thrown past the racket is not a serve, the hit must add speed: 0.05 s after its last contact with the racket the ball must be faster than it was when it reached the racket; and the ball may move at most 5.0 m/s when it reaches the racket (the speed of a ball that has fallen about 1.3 m: a toss, not a throw)
Rule 4 (the racket in the hand): the racket is clamped to the right hand with its handle along the forearm (the hand has no fingers to change the grip); it cannot be dropped or thrown
Rule 12 (a ball touching a line is in): the ball's footprint is one point, the point under its centre at its first contact with the ground (a real ball's footprint is about 5 cm across)

Rule 24 f (deliberately touching the ball twice, carrying it): intention cannot be judged: racket contacts less than 0.05 s apart are one hit, a later one is a second hit, and a contact longer than 0.05 s is a carry
Rule 1 (the net): a 2 cm thick wall instead of a mesh of cord; a ball that meets it is stopped by a stiff, strongly damped contact
wind and weather: none; the air is still (sea level, 15 C)

texts.sentence: Serve: from behind your baseline, release the tennis ball in your left hand, strike it with the racket on your right hand before it reaches the ground, and send it over the net into the service box diagonally opposite.
texts.rules: The court is the ITF singles court: 23.77 m long and 8.23 m wide, measured to the outside of the lines, with a service line 6.4 m from the net on each side and a centre service line that divides the space between the net and each service line into two service boxes. The net stands across the middle, 0.914 m high at its centre and rising in a straight line to 1.07 m at the posts, which stand 0.914 m outside the sidelines. The ball is the ITF ball (radius 0.0335 m, 0.0577 kg, with air drag and spin lift) and starts gripped in your left hand; the racket (0.685 m long, 0.30 kg, strung surface 0.33 m by 0.25 m) is fixed to your right hand. You serve from the right of the centre mark into the far service box on the left of the centre line. In order: (1) the toss: you let go of the ball (the grip takes a ball only once) while you stand at rest, both feet on the ground behind the baseline, between the extension of the centre mark and the extension of the right sideline, neither foot having left the ground or moved more than 0.02 m in the last 0.5 s (so not before 0.5 s after the start); (2) the strike: your racket hits the ball before it reaches the ground (any part of the racket counts), the ball having touched nothing of you for the last 0.1 s and moving at most 5.0 m/s when it reaches the racket (a toss, not a throw), and the hit speeds the ball up (0.05 s after its last contact with the racket it is faster than it was when it reached the racket); (3) the ball's centre passes the net's plane between the posts above the net's top edge; (4) its first contact with the ground is inside that service box, the lines included (the point under the ball's centre decides; ground contacts less than 0.02 s apart are one): that is the success. From the release to the strike your feet may not touch the baseline or the court, the ground beyond the sideline's extension or the centre mark's extension, nor the ground more than 0.3 m from where each stood at the release (a foot fault); after the strike you may step anywhere on your side. A serve that touches the net and still lands in the box is a let: it does not count, and you serve again, under the same rules, with the spare ball (your left hand's grip can take it from then on); this happens at most 1 time(s), a further let fails. You fail on any fault: releasing the ball when not at rest in the server's position, a foot fault, the tossed ball reaching the ground or passing the net unstruck, the racket striking the ball before it is clear of you, a ball that reaches the racket faster than 5.0 m/s, a hit that does not speed it up, the racket touching the struck ball again (contacts less than 0.05 s apart are one hit) or staying on it longer than 0.05 s, the served ball touching you, a net post, the ground on your side or the ground outside the service box, or passing the net's plane anywhere but over the net. You also fail if any part of you or the racket touches the net or a post, if you fall, or after 20 s. A fall is: your pelvis lower than 0.35 m above the ground, or any part of you other than your feet touching the ground; the racket may touch the ground.
texts.venue: You stand as the server: your pelvis 0.5 m behind your baseline and 1.0 m to the right of the centre mark, facing the net (+x), which is 12.385 m ahead of you. Painted on the court, all 0.05 m wide and inside the measurements: the two baselines, the two singles sidelines, the two service lines, the centre service line between them and a 0.10 m centre mark on each baseline; there are no doubles lines. Your target, the far service box on the left of the centre line, begins at the net and ends 6.4 m beyond it, and reaches from the centre service line 4.115 m to the left. The ball lies in your left palm; the spare ball rests in a cup on a thin stand, its centre 0.25 m ahead of your pelvis, 0.6 m to your left and 1.05 m above the ground. The racket's handle lies along your right forearm; its strings face the way your palm faces. A ball is released when the hand's grip is switched off; it leaves with the hand's velocity.
texts.difficulty: The ball must be struck in the air with the strings of a racket that reaches up to 2.7 m, leave at well over 10 m/s in a narrow window of directions to clear a net 11.9 m away and still come down within 6.4 m beyond it, and the swing that gives it that speed must not knock over or move the feet of a body that stands without a balance controller. Both arms have to work in time: the released ball is in the racket's reach for a few tenths of a second.

stand.meaning: the platform holds the legs in the stance; you give the waist's 1 and the arms' 14 joint targets (rad)

walk.meaning: Unitree's walking policy drives the legs from the velocity command (vx forward, vy to the left, m/s; wz turning left, rad/s; the robot's own frame); you give the waist and arm joint targets

joints.meaning: you give all 27 joint targets (rad); the default PD gains, no feed-forward

lowcmd.meaning: Unitree's LowCmd for all 27 joints: position targets (rad), velocity targets (rad/s), feed-forward torques (N m), kp, kd; the motor torque is kp (q - q_measured) + kd (dq - dq_measured) + tau, evaluated at 1 kHz

grip.rule: a closed grip holds the nearest grippable object whose surface is within reach_m of the palm (a point 4.5 cm beyond the wrist flange along the forearm) and that moves no faster than max_relative_speed_m_s relative to it; opening the grip lets it go
